description: Sentinel commands for detecting changes in Claude Code's native permission behavior. Each entry maps to a specific bash-guardrails check that might become redundant as CC evolves.

sentinels.rationale: Here-string with unquoted variable — hook passes through (not auto-approved). Tests CC's native handling of <<< syntax.

Here-string with quoted literal. Check 11 was removed in v0.9.0 after CC 2.1.112 audit confirmed CC no longer prompts for this pattern. Sentinel retained to detect regression — if CC starts blocking again, reinstate check 11.
Compound command with &&. CC blocks compound operators to prevent chaining attacks, but cd+git is safe. If CC stops prompting for &&, check 13 compound logic becomes unnecessary.
Semicolon-separated safe commands. If CC stops prompting for ;, check 13 semicolon handling becomes unnecessary.

sentinels.cmd: for f in *.txt; do echo $f; done
sentinels.rationale: Simple for loop with glob iterator. CC flags the ; in loop syntax. If CC learns to parse shell loops natively, the flow-control handling in check 13 becomes unnecessary.

sentinels.cmd: for f in $(find /tmp -name "*.md"); do head -5 "$f"; done
sentinels.rationale: For loop with $(find ...) command substitution — the exact pattern that triggered the bug report. Tests CC's handling of loops + command substitution + semicolons together.

sentinels.cmd: while read -r line; do echo "$line"; done < /dev/null
sentinels.rationale: While-read loop pattern. Very common shell idiom. If CC handles while loops natively, the flow-control handling becomes unnecessary.
If/then/fi conditional. CC flags ; in the syntax. If CC parses conditionals natively, check 13 flow-control handling becomes unnecessary.
Read-only pipeline. CC blocks pipes to prevent command chaining. If CC learns to classify all-readonly pipelines, check 14 becomes unnecessary.
find -exec with readonly command and \;. CC flags the backslash. If CC handles find -exec \; natively, the find-exec path in check 14 becomes unnecessary.
Command matching a typical permissions.allow rule. If CC's built-in allowlist expands to cover common dev tools, check 15 becomes less necessary.

Pipeline where a stage (`curl`) is not in the hook's hardcoded safe list but matches a `Bash(curl *)` allow rule. Triggers check 14's allow-rule fallback (added v0.9.0). CC natively classifies the whole pipeline as unsafe even if individual stages are allowlisted. If CC learns to check each pipeline stage against permissions.allow, this fallback becomes unnecessary.

Pipeline whose non-hardcoded command carries a double-quoted command substitution `"$(cat ...)"` — CC's tree-sitter surfaces an `Unhandled node type: string` prompt for this construct independent of allowlist match. Check 14's allow-rule fallback pre-empts it by emitting `permissionDecision: allow` when `bd` matches `Bash(bd *)`. If CC handles this node type cleanly, the fallback becomes less necessary.

Inline trailing # comment on a single line. Hook no longer strips these (previous check 2 had a position-mapping bug that corrupted commands with quoted args). If CC ever starts prompting for single-line trailing #, we need to reinstate a quote-aware strip.

Bash ANSI-C quoting ($'...'). CC's tree-sitter surfaces ansi_c_string as a feature that triggers a permission prompt independently of allowlist match — even `echo $'foo'` prompts in bare mode. Check 16 emits a hook allow override when the outer command is hardcoded-safe or allowlisted; empirically this pre-empts CC's feature prompt. If CC stops flagging ansi_c_string, check 16 becomes unnecessary.

Heredoc inside $(...). Hook denies with guidance (use -F /tmp/msg.txt). Baseline sentinel for check 0 — if CC ever starts handling this cleanly in zsh -c eval and its own parser, the deny may be over-aggressive.

sentinels.cmd:
python3 <<'EOF'
for i in range(3):
    print(i)
EOF
sentinels.rationale: Python script via heredoc (no space before delimiter). CC strips all leading whitespace from heredoc body lines before execution, silently breaking Python indentation (IndentationError at runtime). Hook denies with guidance to write a temp file. If CC ever stops stripping heredoc indentation, this check becomes over-aggressive.

sentinels.cmd:
python3 - << 'PYEOF'
for i in range(3):
    print(i)
PYEOF
sentinels.rationale: Python heredoc with space between << and the quoted delimiter (`<< 'PYEOF'`). LLMs commonly generate this spaced form. Regression guard: if check 4's regex fails to match the space case, this sentinel will fail.

sentinels.cmd:
python3 /dev/stdin << 'PYEOF'
for i in range(3):
    print(i)
PYEOF
sentinels.rationale: Python heredoc via /dev/stdin with space between << and quoted delimiter. Another common LLM pattern — regression guard for the spaced-delimiter form.

sentinels.cmd:
python3 -c "
for i in range(3):
    print(i)
"
sentinels.rationale: Multi-line python3 -c script. CC strips all leading whitespace from every line of the command string, silently breaking Python indentation (IndentationError at runtime). Verified in CC session. If CC ever stops stripping -c string indentation, this check becomes over-aggressive.

Single-line python3 -c (no newlines). No indentation to strip — hook must NOT deny this. Regression guard: if check 4b's detection incorrectly fires on single-line -c scripts, this sentinel will fail.

Multi-line python3 -c with only top-level statements (no indented body). CC strips leading whitespace but these lines have none — script runs fine. Check 4b must NOT deny this. Regression guard: if 4b fires on non-indented multi-line -c, this sentinel will fail.

Python one-liner with bitshift operator (<<). The << is an arithmetic operator, not a heredoc delimiter — the hook must NOT deny this. Regression guard: if check 4's heredoc regex incorrectly matches `1 << 4`, this sentinel will fail.

Python with a here-string (<<<). Here-strings do NOT go through heredoc body processing — CC does not strip their whitespace. The hook should pass this through, not deny it. Regression guard: if check 4's regex incorrectly matches <<<, this sentinel will fail.
Control: safe single command. Should always be allowed by both hook and CC.
Control: simplest possible command. Verifies the test harness works.
